bigpic.b: Asian stocks bounce before Wall Street reopens
bigpic.t: with the Kospi up 2.2% and US futures higher, even as markets price a near-certain Fed hike on 9 Dec.

bigpic.b: Oil holds near $96 after Saudi refinery strikes
bigpic.t: as a hit on Jazan follows attacks on Ras Tanura and mines off Oman, two days before OPEC+ meets.

bigpic.b: Nvidia is under scrutiny on two fronts
bigpic.t: as S&P weighs a governance-driven rating cut and Southeast Asian banks vet who uses its AI chips.

stories.h: Asian stocks rebound as the Kospi jumps 2.2% before Wall Street's half-day session
stories.sum: In Friday morning trade the Kospi rose 2.2% to 4,812.65 and the Nikkei 225 gained 0.7% to 57,919.30 as AI-linked shares recovered from an early-week rout. Hong Kong added 0.4% while Shanghai slipped 0.1%. US stock futures were about 0.6% higher ahead of a shortened session ending at 1pm ET.
stories.why: Investors are testing whether November's tech sell-off has run its course before next week's jobs data and a likely Fed hike.

stories.h: China's industrial profits jump 20.1% in October as electronics makers lead
stories.sum: Profits at large Chinese industrial firms rose 20.1% from a year earlier in October, up from 14.4% in September, statistics bureau data show. Profits for January to October rose 16%. Computer, telecom and electronic equipment makers roughly doubled their profits over the ten months, while furniture makers' profits fell about 52%.
stories.why: AI hardware is lifting Chinese factory earnings, but weak home demand leaves firms leaning on exports that face new US tariffs.

stories.h: US PCE inflation hits 3.8% in October as third-quarter growth is revised up to 4.3%
stories.sum: The Fed's preferred price gauge rose 0.3% on the month and 3.8% from a year earlier, while core prices climbed 3.3%, a tenth above forecasts. Third-quarter GDP growth was revised to an annualised 4.3% from 3.4%. Consumer spending was flat after inflation and the saving rate stood at 4.1%.
stories.why: Hot prices alongside strong growth make a Fed hike on 9 December near certain, pushing borrowing costs higher across the economy.

stories.h: Nvidia pauses Southeast Asia server shipments while it checks export compliance
stories.sum: Nvidia told partners including Dell and Super Micro to halt server deliveries to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia for an unspecified period, the Wall Street Journal reported, while it checks customers meet US rules. Commerce closed a loophole that let Chinese firms use such chips remotely; one estimate says these sites supply about 24% of China's AI computing.
stories.why: Southeast Asia's data-centre build-out relies on steady Nvidia supply, so a long pause could stall projects and their financing.

stories.h: S&P puts Nvidia's AA rating on watch for a cut, citing board oversight concerns
stories.sum: S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch negative on 25 Nov and flagged a likely one-notch cut within 90 days. It questioned board independence, oversight of the chief executive and succession planning after Jensen Huang resigned on 12 Nov and was reinstated on 23 Nov. Moody's kept its Aa1 rating with a stable outlook.
stories.why: A governance-driven downgrade would add to investor unease over the company at the centre of AI spending.

stories.h: Kioxia jumps as much as 14.5% after Nvidia tests its SSDs as extra AI memory
stories.sum: Kioxia and Nvidia are testing a setup that puts 144 Kioxia SSDs, about 1.1 petabytes of raw storage, in a GB200 NVL72 system to handle a database of 2 trillion vectors. The aim is to reduce reliance on costly high-bandwidth memory. Kioxia shares rose as much as 14.5% to 7,895 yen on 26 Nov.
stories.why: Using flash storage as a memory tier could ease the HBM bottleneck in AI servers and lift demand for NAND chips.

stories.h: Bank of Korea raises its key rate to 3.25% and signals more hikes ahead
stories.sum: The Bank of Korea lifted its base rate by a quarter point to 3.25% on 26 Nov, the highest in two years, in a 5 to 2 vote at its last meeting of 2026. It raised its domestic growth estimates, and Governor Hyun Song Shin said further increases were likely.
stories.why: Seoul joins the ECB, and probably the Fed, in tightening, lifting borrowing costs for Korean households and companies.

stories.h: Tokyo core inflation hits 2.9%, a 16-month high, ahead of the BOJ's December meeting
stories.sum: Consumer prices in Tokyo excluding fresh food rose 2.9% from a year earlier in November, up from 2.6% and the fastest since July 2025, though just below the 3.0% forecast. Headline inflation was 2.8%, and the measure that also strips out energy rose 2.5%.
stories.why: Tokyo figures lead national data, so faster inflation strengthens the case for a Bank of Japan rate rise on 18 Dec.

stories.h: Eurozone leaders back Spain's Hernández de Cos to succeed Lagarde at the ECB
stories.sum: Leaders meeting in Brussels on 26 Nov favoured the Bank for International Settlements chief over Klaas Knot. He would be the first Spaniard to lead the ECB when Lagarde leaves on 7 Feb 2027, after formal steps including consulting the European Parliament. France's Laurence Boone is expected to take Isabel Schnabel's markets role.
stories.why: Markets read the choice as policy continuity at a bank that has raised rates twice this year with inflation at 4%.

stories.h: Bitcoin tops $61,000 as Nasdaq futures extend Wednesday’s rebound
Bitcoin edges above $61,000 ahead of the expiry of $7B of Deribit options
stories.sum: Bitcoin traded near $61,300 on Friday afternoon in Asia, up about 1%, before roughly $7B of Deribit options expire at 08:00 UTC, 4pm in Singapore. Positioning is more defensive than in October, with a put-to-call ratio of 0.89 against 0.55. US spot bitcoin ETFs have lost about $5.39B in November, a monthly record.
stories.why: Steady fund selling has removed a key source of demand, leaving prices exposed to swings around large derivatives expiries.

stories.h: Switzerland's first spot bitcoin ETF starts trading on the SIX exchange
stories.sum: BIT Asset Management listed BBIT on the SIX Swiss Exchange on 26 Nov, seeded with 350 bitcoin worth over $20M and charging 0.19% a year. Swiss regulator FINMA approved it on 20 Oct after an 18-month review and exempted it from diversification rules. BIT says it is Europe's only active spot bitcoin ETF.
stories.why: A regulated ETF wrapper gives Swiss wealth managers a simpler route into bitcoin, even as US funds see record outflows.

stories.h: New York wins $1.37B judgment against NovaTech founders over crypto fraud
stories.sum: A New York state court ordered Cynthia and Eddie Petion, founders of NovaTechFx and AWS Mining, to pay $1.37B. The SEC says NovaTech raised about $650M from more than 200,000 investors between 2019 and 2023, and victims included 11,000 New Yorkers, many recruited through church groups and social media. The couple have left the US.
stories.why: The award shows state regulators pursuing crypto investment schemes hard, though collecting from founders abroad will be difficult.

stories.h: FDA delays its decision on Vertex's kidney drug povetacicept to February
stories.sum: The FDA extended its review of povetacicept for IgA nephropathy by up to three months, moving the target date from 30 Nov to no later than 28 Feb 2027. It classed Vertex's response to a late information request as a major amendment. The drug blocks two immune signalling proteins, BAFF and APRIL.
stories.why: The delay holds back a key growth product as Vertex tries to expand beyond its cystic fibrosis franchise.

stories.h: FDA approves Roche's Wilserdly, first new early breast cancer hormone pill in 20 years
stories.sum: The FDA cleared giredestrant on 23 Nov as a once-daily pill after surgery for ER-positive, HER2-negative stage I to III breast cancer at intermediate or high risk of returning. In the 4,170-patient lidERA trial it cut the risk of invasive recurrence or death by 30% compared with standard hormone therapy.
stories.why: About 90% of HR-positive, HER2-negative cases are found early, giving Roche a large market for years of daily treatment.

stories.h: Sanofi agrees to buy Insmed for $41B in pharma's biggest deal since 2023
stories.sum: Sanofi will pay $175 a share, a 46% premium to Insmed's 18 Nov price, gaining Brinsupri for bronchiectasis, with $1.09B of sales in the first nine months, plus Arikayce and the Phase 3 lung drug TPIP. Closing is expected in the first half of 2027. Sanofi shares rose 9.8% on 24 Nov and 4.9% on 25 Nov after upgrades.
stories.why: Gives Sanofi new respiratory growth before Dupixent, about 40% of group revenue, loses its main US patent in 2031.

stories.h: Brent holds near $96 as a strike on a Saudi refinery adds to Gulf supply fears
stories.sum: Brent eased 0.3% to $96.29 a barrel in early Asian trade on Friday after Thursday's 2.1% gain, while WTI rose 2.1% to $85.43 as it caught up after the US holiday. A projectile hit Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery on Thursday, killing one worker, following Houthi claims on Ras Tanura and Iranian reports of tankers hitting mines off Oman.
stories.why: Attacks on Saudi refineries and mines near Hormuz keep a war premium in crude two days before OPEC+ meets.
src: Economic Times via The Fifth Skill

stories.h: OPEC+ likely to roll over output targets into 2027 at Sunday's meetings
stories.sum: Two sources told Reuters the group will probably keep current targets for at least the first quarter of 2027 when ministers meet from 1300 GMT on 29 Nov, though nothing is decided. Its first capacity review is unsettled: Iraq rejects a preliminary 4.9M barrels a day and Kazakhstan wants more. Rystad sees a 2027 surplus near 5M barrels a day.
stories.why: Holding quotas steady postpones a fight over capacity-based shares as the market heads toward a large surplus.

stories.h: Boehly's Eldridge leads a US-backed deal for Lukoil's international assets
stories.sum: A consortium led by Todd Boehly's Eldridge, including the US International Development Finance Corporation, UAE-based Catena Investment Holding and Xtellus Partners, agreed on 25 Nov to take over Lukoil's foreign business. It spans oil and gas assets in Bulgaria, Romania, Africa and the Middle East plus fuel stations abroad. No price was given; US Treasury approval is still required.
stories.why: The deal would move refineries and oilfields out of sanctioned Russian ownership, with Washington taking a stake through the DFC.

stories.h: Guangzhou Auto Show opens with established carmakers leading launches as sales slump
stories.sum: The show opened on 27 Nov with 1,106 vehicles. BMW, BYD and GAC Honda hold many premiere slots, while start-ups such as NIO, XPeng and Xiaomi have no all-new models on the list and mostly skipped media-day events. BYD's Yangwang brand showed a 2.08M yuan limousine. China's October passenger car retail sales fell 27.1% from a year earlier.
stories.why: With demand shrinking and a price war under way, carmakers are betting on premium and tech-heavy models to win buyers.

stories.h: BYD enters exclusive talks to buy Ineos's Hambach car plant in France
stories.sum: BYD confirmed exclusive negotiations for the factory, which can build about 30,000 Grenadier off-roaders a year and employs roughly 1,000 people. It would be BYD's second EU car plant after Hungary. Ineos, which has invested nearly €540M in the site since 2019, plans to move Grenadier production to the US, its main market, from 2028.
stories.why: A French plant would let BYD build inside the EU and sidestep the extra duties on Chinese-made electric cars.

stories.h: EU caps Chinese-built hybrid imports at 191,780 cars until June
stories.sum: The EU adopted provisional quotas on 24 Nov limiting hybrid imports from China and other countries from 1 Dec to 18 Jun 2027. China-built plug-in, full and mild hybrids share a cap of 191,780 cars across three periods, while range-extended EVs and EU-built hybrids fall outside it. China's commerce ministry reserved the right to challenge the move at the WTO.
stories.why: Hybrids escaped the EU's extra duties on Chinese electric cars, so quotas narrow a key path into Europe for Chinese brands.

stories.h: Japan Tobacco shares rise 4% on report it may join a bid for Imperial Brands
stories.sum: Japan Tobacco rose 4.1% to 5,754 yen in Tokyo on Friday after Bloomberg reported it is weighing a bid for Imperial with a partner. Altria said on Thursday it may make an all-cash offer and is talking to another party about part of Imperial, which jumped about 13% to a £25.9B value. Imperial says it has had no approach.
stories.why: A two-buyer carve-up could reshape global tobacco, though Japan Tobacco is also absorbing an $8.7B loss on seized Russian units.

stories.h: US online holiday spending tops $82.5B so far, up 9.1%, Adobe says
stories.sum: Shoppers spent more than $82.5B online from 1 to 22 Nov, and buy now, pay later spending rose 6.5% to $6.1B, Adobe Analytics data show. Adobe expects $6.9B on Thanksgiving, $12.9B on Black Friday and $15.1B on Cyber Monday. Visits to retail sites referred by AI assistants are up 127%.
stories.why: Solid online demand into the holiday peak supports retailers' fourth-quarter forecasts despite inflation running near 4%.

stories.h: Poundland falls into administration, putting about 11,000 jobs at risk
stories.sum: The UK discount chain appointed AlixPartners as administrators on 25 Nov after sale talks with bidders including Martin Property Group failed to find a solvent deal. Its roughly 600 stores keep trading while buyers are sought, and Tesco and B&M are reported to be interested in parts. Owner Gordon Brothers bought Poundland for £1 last year.
stories.why: A break-up would let rivals such as Tesco and B&M pick up sites, reshaping Britain's discount high street before Christmas.

stories.h: Sunrise on the Reaping takes $15M on Thanksgiving eve as Hexed and Focker In-Law lag
stories.sum: Lionsgate's Hunger Games prequel earned $15M on Wednesday and is tracking $85M over five days, which would lift its domestic total to $233M. Disney's Hexed opened with $7.6M and a $31M to $35M five-day forecast, while Universal's Focker In-Law took $5.3M. Both had been expected to reach $40M to $45M.
stories.why: Soft starts for two costly holiday releases, including Hexed at over $200M, add pressure on studios' original and comedy bets.

stories.h: Netflix buys Los Angeles's 1928 Radford Studio Center for a reported $380M
stories.sum: Netflix said on 24 Nov it is purchasing the Studio City lot and will keep the existing studio team. The 55-acre site was bought for $1.85B in 2021 by Hackman Capital Partners and Square Mile Capital before falling into foreclosure, so the reported price is a steep discount.
stories.why: Owning a historic lot cheaply secures Netflix production space in Los Angeles as distressed studio property changes hands.

stories.h: Norse Atlantic stays grounded with no buyer named as staff go unpaid
stories.sum: The Norwegian long-haul carrier halted all flights on 26 Nov and says it will file for bankruptcy unless it secures emergency funding; takeover talks have produced no named buyer. Staff were told salaries could not be paid, the ITF says, and winter routes to Bangkok and Phuket are in doubt. Its shares fell 85% on 25 Nov.
stories.why: Jet fuel costs tied to the Middle East war are pushing thinly funded long-haul airlines out, cutting low-fare capacity.

stories.h: Poland to sign deal for Palantir's Maven military AI software on Friday
stories.sum: Poland's defence ministry said it will sign an agreement with Palantir on 27 Nov to buy AI software that supports military decision-making. The Maven Smart System will run in Poland as Saturn, and the ministry says Palantir gets no access to military data or encryption keys. No value was disclosed; critics had called for an open tender.
stories.why: The purchase extends Palantir's reach in European defence as front-line NATO states spend more on AI planning tools.

stories.h: US proposes a 10% tariff on Brazilian aircraft, ending Embraer's exemption
stories.sum: USTR proposed on 25 Nov a 10% duty on finished aircraft from Brazil, including planes and helicopters, ending an exemption granted in July when a 25% tariff hit other Brazilian goods. Comments run from 27 Nov to 30 Dec, with a hearing on 14 Jan. Embraer, which supplies E175 regional jets to US carriers, fell as much as 9.2%.
stories.why: A duty would raise costs for US regional airlines flying Embraer jets and break with the industry's tradition of tariff-free aircraft trade.

stories.h: Vanke asks bondholders to vote on 8 Dec on a second delay for a 1.2B yuan note
stories.sum: China Vanke wants to push back repayment of about 1.2B yuan ($180M) of a note due 15 Dec by another three years, its second extension on the bond, with a vote set for 8 Dec. Sources say any upfront cash payment may be well below the 40% paid in the first extension.
stories.why: Repeated extensions at a developer backed by state-owned Shenzhen Metro test how far Beijing will go to avoid a default.

stories.h: IOI Properties buys Singapore's Shenton House from its CEO's company for S$593M
stories.sum: The Malaysian developer is acquiring the 25-storey office block in Singapore's business district from Shenton 101, a private firm owned by chief executive Lee Yeow Seng, paying S$217M and taking on about S$376M of debt. It plans a 35-storey mixed-use tower with a 165-room hotel, built from 2027 to 2031.
stories.why: The related-party deal deepens IOI's bet on Singapore, where it now owns almost US$8B of property.

stories.h: US new home sales jump 14.2% in October despite 7% mortgage rates
stories.sum: Sales of new single-family homes rose to an annual rate of 701,000 in October from a downwardly revised 614,000 in September, Census data show, and were 7.5% higher than a year earlier. Supply fell to eight months, the lowest this year. Year-to-date sales remain 3% behind 2025, the National Association of Home Builders says.
stories.why: A surprise rebound offers builders some relief, though high rates keep resale activity near decade lows.

stories.h: Banks tighten checks on Singapore and Malaysia data-centre borrowers over US chip rule
stories.sum: Citigroup and Standard Chartered have joined DBS, OCBC and UOB in reviewing Southeast Asian data-centre clients, asking them to show who uses their AI chips, Bloomberg reported. A $480M loan for an Aolani Cloud site in Malaysia has stalled. MAS said it expects banks to stay vigilant, and OCBC sees no material concerns.
stories.why: Tighter lending could slow Johor's and Singapore's data-centre pipeline just as Nvidia pauses server deliveries to the region.

stories.h: Singapore factory output rises 6.1% in October on AI-driven chip equipment demand
stories.sum: Manufacturing output grew 6.1% from a year earlier in October, up from 5% in September, EDB data show, and 12.1% excluding biomedical products. Precision engineering surged 54.1% on semiconductor equipment and electronics rose 6.6%, while biomedical output fell 35.8%. Seasonally adjusted output jumped 7.1% from September.
stories.why: Strong AI-linked production underpins the government's raised 2026 growth forecast before an expected slowdown next year.

stories.h: Malaysian think tank sees 2026 growth of 5% to 5.5% as US weighs tariffs up to 18%
stories.sum: The Malaysian Institute of Economic Research forecast 2026 growth of 5.0% to 5.5%, above the official 4.8% to 5.3% range, with the fourth quarter easing to 4.5% to 5.0% after 5.5% in the third. It expects 4.2% to 5.2% in 2027. The US has proposed extra duties of up to 18% on Malaysian goods.
stories.why: Exports, especially AI-linked electronics, drive Malaysian growth, so new US duties would hit the economy's main engine.

stories.h: Malaysia says it has made no commitment to rescue AirAsia
stories.sum: Second Finance Minister Amir Hamzah Azizan told parliament on 26 Nov the government has agreed no loan guarantees or capital injections for AirAsia, though domestic air links remain a priority. Any help would follow the Vantris model, putting the state ahead of lenders. AirAsia handled nearly 60% of domestic passengers at MAHB airports in 2025.
stories.why: AirAsia dominates flights to Sabah and Sarawak, so its funding gap is a public concern with jet fuel above $200 a barrel.
